{ "source": "{% extends 'OT Layout' %} {% block content %} {% comment %} My Work dashboard (PP-03). Scoped to the signed-in contact through al_ReviewInstance.al_assignedcontactid and al_RemediationAction.al_assignedcontactid (AD-047, AD-050). Those lookups landed with the Phase 2 schema delta, so the shell-stage note this page used to carry is gone. Scoping here is presentation, never a boundary. Under OD-022 every authenticated user may read every case, and the write boundary is the Contact-anchored table permission chain (AD-056, AD-069) - not this filter. What the filter buys is a worklist that shows the reviewer their own work instead of the whole environment. {% endcomment %} {% comment %} user is null for an anonymous visitor. Home carries a Restrict Read rule (AD-068) so a signed-out request should never reach this page, but an unguarded {{ user.id }} would emit an empty condition value and silently count every row in the table - the exact over-report this page exists to stop. Fail closed instead. {% endcomment %} {% if user == null %} {% include 'OT Empty State' title: 'Sign in to see your work' message: 'This page shows the reviews and remediation actions assigned to you.' %} {% else %} {% assign me = user.id %} {% comment %} Search and filters (PP-03, project owner 2026-09-10). Three parameters: `ref` is a contains-match on the case reference, `check` narrows to one discipline, and `state` separates what you still owe from what you have already submitted. Applied in the fetch, not over the rendered rows. The table takes the first 25 reviews, so a filter in the browser would search the 25 that happened to load and silently miss the review being looked for - the same reasoning the review list records for its own search. `check` and `state` are tested against the values they are allowed to be, which is what the review list does with `mine`. An unrecognised value becomes no filter rather than a condition, so nothing typed into the URL reaches the FetchXML. `ref` cannot be an allowlist, so it is xml_escaped at the point it is used. The counts above are deliberately not filtered. They answer "how much work do I have", which does not change because the table below is being searched - a tile that moved with the filter would be a second, quieter answer to a question the page already answers. {% endcomment %} {% assign f_ref = request.params['ref'] | default: '' %} {% assign f_check = request.params['check'] | default: '' %} {% if f_check != 'tax' and f_check != 'aqs' %}{% assign f_check = '' %}{% endif %} {% assign f_state = request.params['state'] | default: '' %} {% if f_state != 'open' and f_state != 'done' %}{% assign f_state = '' %}{% endif %} {% assign filtered = false %} {% if f_ref != '' or f_check != '' or f_state != '' %}{% assign filtered = true %}{% endif %} {% fetchxml case_count %} {% endfetchxml %} {% fetchxml review_count %} {% endfetchxml %} {% comment %} Submitted reviews, counted separately from the outstanding ones above. The outstanding tile is labelled "Reviews to complete" and must keep counting only what is still to do, so this is a fourth count rather than a widened one. {% endcomment %} {% fetchxml submitted_count %} {% endfetchxml %} {% fetchxml remediation_count %} {% endfetchxml %} {% comment %} Every review assigned to this contact, submitted or not. This list used to carry a second condition, al_submittedon is null, on the reasoning that a submitted review is finished work and belongs on the review list rather than on a to-do. What that actually produced was a review vanishing from the page at the moment it was submitted, with nothing on My Work left to say it had been - so the one place a checker looks after submitting was the one place that no longer mentioned the review. The case-level views could not fill the gap either: CaseTransitions.MoveThrough hops the case through Submitted to its destination in the same transaction (OutcomeRules.HopsFor), so no case list ever rests on "Submitted" and the review row is the only record of it. A submitted review stays here, badged Submitted and carrying its submitted date, and its link opens the same read-only questionnaire the review page already renders for a locked review (PP-11). The tile above still counts only what is outstanding, because its label says "Reviews to complete". Ordered submitted-last (al_submittedon ascending sorts nulls first), then by case due date so the most pressing outstanding review still sits at the top. {% endcomment %} {% fetchxml my_reviews %} {% if f_check == 'tax' %}{% endif %} {% if f_check == 'aqs' %}{% endif %} {% if f_state == 'open' %}{% endif %} {% if f_state == 'done' %}{% endif %} {% comment %} The reference names the linked case by alias, which is what the case list already does for its outcome filter - and the link below is an inner one, so a review whose case is missing drops out of a search rather than surviving it as a blank row. {% endcomment %} {% if f_ref != '' %}{% endif %} {% endfetchxml %} {% comment %} An aggregate fetch returns no result set at all when the caller cannot read the table — an anonymous visitor, or a signed-in user whose web role grants nothing on it. Indexing entities[0] straight away then fails with "Index was outside the bounds of the array", and the tile renders that message as its label. A `default` filter cannot save it: the index is evaluated before any filter runs, so the guard has to come first. Same .size > 0 test the case table below already uses. {% endcomment %} {% assign total_cases = 0 %} {% if case_count.results and case_count.results.entities.size > 0 %} {% assign total_cases = case_count.results.entities[0].total %} {% endif %} {% assign total_reviews = 0 %} {% if review_count.results and review_count.results.entities.size > 0 %} {% assign total_reviews = review_count.results.entities[0].total %} {% endif %} {% assign total_submitted = 0 %} {% if submitted_count.results and submitted_count.results.entities.size > 0 %} {% assign total_submitted = submitted_count.results.entities[0].total %} {% endif %} {% assign total_remediations = 0 %} {% if remediation_count.results and remediation_count.results.entities.size > 0 %} {% assign total_remediations = remediation_count.results.entities[0].total %} {% endif %}
  • {% comment %} Scoped, because the count above is scoped. This tile used to link to /cases, which renders every case in the environment - a tile reading nine that opened a list of thirteen. The list honours ?mine=1 and offers All cases as a deliberate second click. {% endcomment %} {{ total_cases }} My cases
  • {{ total_reviews }} Reviews to complete
  • {% comment %} Lands on the reviews table further down this page, which is where a submitted review now lives - there is no review list page that filters to submitted, and a tile that opens the whole discipline would not be the set it counted. Every tile on this page goes somewhere; a card that only displays a number reads as broken. It carries state=done, so the table it lands on holds exactly the reviews this tile counted. Before the filter existed the link could only scroll to a table that also held the outstanding ones, which is the gap the comment above describes. {% endcomment %} {{ total_submitted }} Reviews you have submitted
  • {{ total_remediations }} Open remediation actions
